stem.en: Kabir asks why the polymerase "does not go slower and make no mistakes at all". What does the sim show as you slow down?

text.en: Slower helps, up to a point, and then the error rate stops falling: the wrong nucleotide sometimes fits well enough to pass, however long you look. Meanwhile a cell that copies too slowly is out-divided. The real rate is a compromise. And, from tomorrow's what-if, zero would be a disaster of its own.

feedback.en: A wrong base can pair well enough to fool any check for an instant. Some slips get through at any speed.
Faster is less accurate; the sim shows it. Speed is traded against care.
Nothing is on purpose. The rate is where checking's cost and benefit balance, and it happens to leave a few slips.

explanation.en: Checking costs time and coins. Past a point it buys nothing. The surviving rate is what selection has settled on, and it is not zero.
